body_text:
The intersection $\bigcap_{i \in I} W_i$ of any family of
subspaces of $V$ is itself a subspace of $V$.

*Proof*: Since each $W_i$ is a subspace, $0 \in W_i$ for all
$i \in I$, so $0 \in \bigcap_{i \in I} W_i$. If
$u, v \in \bigcap_{i \in I} W_i$ and $\alpha, \beta \in F$, then
for each $i \in I$, $u, v \in W_i$. Since each $W_i$ is a
subspace, $\alpha u + \beta v \in W_i$ for every $i \in I$.
Therefore, $\alpha u + \beta v \in \bigcap_{i \in I} W_i$.

Consequently, the span $\operatorname{span}(S)$ of any subset
$S \subseteq V$ coincides with the intersection of all subspaces
of $V$ that contain $S$, which is precisely the set of all finite
linear combinations of vectors in $S$.
